description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 while verifying that LEAPR can regenerate graphite S(alpha,beta) from its 12 KB deck.

THE FINDING. Regenerating ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (EVAL-SEP17) and comparing MF=7/MT=4 against the
official tape:

  with bk = 8.617385e-5 eV/K    (NJOY's pre-2018 value):  max rel dev 4.917e-6, RMS 6.390e-7   <- printed precision
  with bk = 8.617333262e-5 eV/K (crate default, CODATA2018): max 3.711e-4, RMS 6.842e-5        <- 100x worse

The ENTIRE difference is the Boltzmann constant. NJOY carried bk = 8.617385e-5 until 23 Oct 2017 (git-confirmed);
this evaluation is EVAL-SEP17, i.e. generated before that change.

WHY THE GOOD FIGURE IS THE RIGHT ONE, demonstrated rather than asserted: endout stores values >= 1e-9 with 7
significant figures and below with 6, which caps relative error at 5e-7 and 5e-6 respectively. Split the residual at
that boundary: 7-fig band max 4.948e-7 against a 5.0e-7 ceiling; 6-fig band max 4.917e-6 against 5.0e-6. Each sits at
99% of its OWN ceiling and neither exceeds it. A physics error would not respect a boundary defined by how a number
was printed. Zero pattern also matches exactly (6645/6645 at 296 K, 6328/6328 at 1000 K, zero mismatches either way).

WHAT THIS MEANS BEYOND GRAPHITE. Any attempt to reproduce a pre-2018 evaluation byte-for-byte needs the era's
constant as an INPUT, not the modern one. This is a general property of regenerating historical nuclear data and it
will recur for every other tsl-* evaluation of that vintage -- and, plausibly, for non-thermal data too.

WHAT TO DECIDE:
  - Make the physical-constant set an explicit, documented input to LEAPR regeneration rather than a compile-time
    constant, so an evaluation's vintage selects it.
  - Decide where the vintage comes from. The tape's own EVAL-SEP17 field is the honest source; hardcoding a date
    cutoff would be a second invented constant.
  - Do NOT quietly change the crate's default bk to the old value. The modern constant is correct for new
    calculations; the old one is correct only for reproducing old evaluations. Conflating them would trade a visible
    100x parity gap for an invisible physics error everywhere else.

Both figures are asserted in tests/leapr_graphite_deck_parity.rs, so neither is hidden and a regression in either
direction fails loudly.

Related: op-hc2o (HTR-10 graphite S(alpha,beta) end-to-end).
title: njoy: reproducing a pre-2018 ENDF evaluation needs that era's Boltzmann constant, not CODATA2018

notes.content:
2026-07-20 (worktree agent-a05077f075edc4722): landed the MF=31/33 covariance
reader, the prerequisite gap noted in the previous comment. New file
src/errorr/covariance.rs (~350 lines): read_covariance_section (faithful port
of covcal's ENDF I/O staging phase, errorr.f90:1868-2060) walks a section's
NL subsections and their NC/NI sub-subsections, returning every raw field
(XMF1/XLFS1/MAT1/MT1, LTY, LS/LB, the flat data array) without decoding
LB-tagged matrix layouts or computing any covariance value -- that group-
average interpretation (errorr.f90:2086-2417) needs the union energy grid
(gridd, errorr.f90:1091-1483, still not ported) and is fused into covcal's
per-group-pair loop rather than separable. Also detect_endf_version
(errorr.f90:456-466, the iverf format-era check MF=31/33 reading depends on).
Cross-checked field-by-field against the real n-092_U_235-ENDF8.0.endf tape
(MAT=9228): MF=33/MT=1 (7-line NC-type LTY=0 "sum of components" section) and
MF=33/MT=2 (NL=9, first subsection NI-type LB=5/LS=1/NT=113050/NP=475, and
113050 == 475*476/2 confirms the symmetric-pack read). 2 new #[cfg(test)]
structural round-trip tests (synthetic + real-tape), both green; full
errorr:: suite 30/30 green; cargo check -p njoy-outram-park-fork --lib
--release clean, no warnings. Wired into errorr/mod.rs's pub API and the
module doc header; errorr/README.md updated to match (was "Not yet ported").

STILL NOT PORTED (unchanged from before, now narrower): covcal's numeric
group-average stage (needs gridd/union grid), grpav/grpav4, colaps/covout,
resprx/rpxsamm resonance-param covariance chain. MF=34/35/40 use different
subsection layouts, not covered by this reader. Legacy ENDF/B-IV (iverf==4)
covariance layout explicitly NotPorted (SubsectionFormat::EndfFormatIv) --
no test tape exercises it. All AI draft, untrusted until Opus V&V pass.

description:
GeN-Foam (gitlab.com/foam-for-nuclear/GeN-Foam, cloned OK to /opt/foam/GeN-Foam) declares in its README that it is built on the OpenFOAM ESI/OpenCFD distribution, currently v2506 (openfoam.com) — NOT the OpenFOAM Foundation 'dev' distribution (openfoam.org) that this repo vendors at crates/outram-foam-turbulence-lib/upstream_source/OpenFOAM. The two distributions are API-incompatible for a solver as deeply integrated as GeN-Foam.

Blocker: the remote-execution container's network policy denies both dl.openfoam.com and develop.openfoam.com (agent proxy returns 403 to CONNECT). github.com and gitlab.com ARE reachable. There is no official ESI mirror on those hosts, and pulling an unofficial third-party mirror was deliberately NOT done — provenance/licence review is required per RESEARCH_INTEGRITY_AND_PROVENANCE.md, so an unverified mirror is not acceptable for this project.

Consequence: GeN-Foam cannot be compiled or run in this container. This is an environment constraint, not a code defect.

What WAS delivered instead (commit ce4bd82): the OUTRAM PARK equivalent V&V case for GeN-Foam's Tutorials/guidedCases/1_reactorSlab_1D_1Gr_neutronicDiffusion, built from that tutorial's nuclearData verbatim (D=0.1275, sigmaRemoval=5.0082, nuSigmaEff=5.5675, P0 scatter 0.1, IV, 6-group beta/lambda) on a 151-cell 1.5 m slab. It verifies against the closed-form one-group bare-slab solution: k_eff = 1.000008 vs analytical 1.000004 (0.4 pcm), and reproduces the k_inf = 1.111677 quoted in the upstream README — confirming the in-group-scattering convention matches.

To unblock: either (a) allowlist dl.openfoam.com / develop.openfoam.com for this environment, or (b) build on a machine with ESI OpenFOAM v2506 already installed, or (c) run the GeN-Foam tutorial elsewhere and commit its reference output as a stored benchmark for regression comparison.
title: GeN-Foam build blocked in container: ESI OpenFOAM v2506 unreachable
